Across Singapore's heartlands, a quiet movement is gaining momentum—ordinary residents transforming their HDB flats into hubs of enterprise. In an age where loneliness is common and connection feels like currency, a new kind of companion has arrived on the market: the AI chatbot. Always awake, always responsive, always affirming. But how much of a real friend or companion can something digital ever be? Our series follows four individuals here in Singapore – different in age, culture, circumstance, yet united by a willingness to explore something different. Over the course of two weeks, each participant shapes their own “ideal” AI companion and introduces it into their life. We witness the ups and downs of these encounters, examining and analysing emotional motivations and algorithmic responses with experts ranging from relationship coaches to AI developers. In the end, the question is: Can AI really fill that human space where a friend or a companion should be?

Twice a year, Asia’s coastlines enter a brief, rare window of extraordinary equinox “king tides” where the Sun, Moon and Earth align and the sea surges beyond its usual limits. In that short period, homes, sea walls, livelihoods and ecosystems are stress-tested and the shoreline becomes a moving border. Tides of Time is a three-part series narrated by BAFTA-nominated presenter and Sunday Times best-selling author Ben Fogle. Filmed in Bangladesh, China and South Korea, the team chases this celestial trigger along three epic shores where water doesn’t just rise but rewrites the communities’ destinies. From Sundarbans’ Hanging Homes Village, to China’s Qiantang “Silver Dragon” tidal bore, to Korea’s getbol mudflats, each film is a human rendezvous with the tide where humans must choose to adapt, resist or surrender.
